question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=e^{x + y},$ $x=4 s^{3}$ and $y=s,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/7e/7e5b5001794ecdf2c9b9e9102f334a63d2c59bc6f7511c2eb7fa358fc94cb0c5.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $s,$ where $x=x(s)$ and $y=y(s),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=e^{x + y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=e^{x + y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =e^{4 s^{3} + s} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =e^{4 s^{3} + s}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}=12 s^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s} \\  & =(e^{4 s^{3} + s})\cdot (12 s^{2})+(e^{4 s^{3} + s})\cdot (1) \\  & =12 s^{2} e^{4 s^{3} + s} + (e^{4 s^{3} + s}) \\  & =(12 s^{2} + 1) e^{4 s^{3} + s}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\sin{(x )} \cos{(y )},$ $x=5 t^{3}$ and $y=t,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\cos{(x )} \cos{(y )},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- \sin{(x )} \sin{(y )}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\cos{(t )} \cos{(5 t^{3} )} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- \sin{(t )} \sin{(5 t^{3} )}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=15 t^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(\cos{(t )} \cos{(5 t^{3} )})\cdot (15 t^{2})+(- \sin{(t )} \sin{(5 t^{3} )})\cdot (1) \\  & =15 t^{2} \cos{(t )} \cos{(5 t^{3} )} - \sin{(t )} \sin{(5 t^{3} )}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=t^{3}$ and $y=t,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =t^{4} e^{t^{4}} + e^{t^{4}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =t^{6} e^{t^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3 t^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(t^{4} e^{t^{4}} + e^{t^{4}})\cdot (3 t^{2})+(t^{6} e^{t^{4}})\cdot (1) \\  & =3 t^{2} e^{t^{4}} + (3 t^{6} e^{t^{4}}) + (t^{6} e^{t^{4}}) \\  & =t^{2} (4 t^{4} + 3) e^{t^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x^{2} e^{y},$ $x=5 t$ and $y=5 t^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2 x e^{y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2 (5 t) e^{(5 t^{2})}=10 t e^{5 t^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(5 t)^{2} e^{(5 t^{2})}=25 t^{2} e^{5 t^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=5,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=10 t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(10 t e^{5 t^{2}})\cdot (5)+(25 t^{2} e^{5 t^{2}})\cdot (10 t) \\  & =50 t e^{5 t^{2}} + (250 t^{3} e^{5 t^{2}}) \\  & =50 t (5 t^{2} + 1) e^{5 t^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x^{2} e^{y},$ $x=3 t$ and $y=t^{4},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2 x e^{y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2 (3 t) e^{(t^{4})}=6 t e^{t^{4}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(3 t)^{2} e^{(t^{4})}=9 t^{2} e^{t^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=4 t^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(6 t e^{t^{4}})\cdot (3)+(9 t^{2} e^{t^{4}})\cdot (4 t^{3}) \\  & =18 t e^{t^{4}} + (36 t^{5} e^{t^{4}}) \\  & =18 t (2 t^{4} + 1) e^{t^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y + 3},$ $x=3 s^{4}$ and $y=s,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}$ where $s + 3\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/7e/7e5b5001794ecdf2c9b9e9102f334a63d2c59bc6f7511c2eb7fa358fc94cb0c5.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $s,$ where $x=x(s)$ and $y=y(s),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{1}{y + 3},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- \frac{x}{(y + 3)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{1}{s + 3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- \frac{3 s^{4}}{(s + 3)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}=12 s^{3},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s} \\  & =(\frac{1}{s + 3})\cdot (12 s^{3})+(- \frac{3 s^{4}}{(s + 3)^{2}})\cdot (1) \\  & =\frac{12 s^{3}}{s + 3} + (- \frac{3 s^{4}}{(s + 3)^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(12 s^{3})(s + 3)-(3 s^{4})(1)}{(s + 3)^2} \\  & =\frac{9 s^{3} (s + 4)}{(s + 3)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y + 4},$ $x=s^{3}$ and $y=s,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}$ where $s + 4\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/7e/7e5b5001794ecdf2c9b9e9102f334a63d2c59bc6f7511c2eb7fa358fc94cb0c5.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $s,$ where $x=x(s)$ and $y=y(s),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{1}{y + 4},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- \frac{x}{(y + 4)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{1}{s + 4} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- \frac{s^{3}}{(s + 4)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}=3 s^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s} \\  & =(\frac{1}{s + 4})\cdot (3 s^{2})+(- \frac{s^{3}}{(s + 4)^{2}})\cdot (1) \\  & =\frac{3 s^{2}}{s + 4} + (- \frac{s^{3}}{(s + 4)^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(3 s^{2})(s + 4)-(s^{3})(1)}{(s + 4)^2} \\  & =\frac{2 s^{2} (s + 6)}{(s + 4)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x \cos{(y )},$ $x=2 t$ and $y=4 t,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\cos{(y )},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- x \sin{(y )}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\cos{(4 t )} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- 2 t \sin{(4 t )}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(\cos{(4 t )})\cdot (2)+(- 2 t \sin{(4 t )})\cdot (4) \\  & =2 (- 4 t \sin{(4 t )} + \cos{(4 t )}).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x^{2} e^{y},$ $x=3 t$ and $y=4 t^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2 x e^{y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2 (3 t) e^{(4 t^{2})}=6 t e^{4 t^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(3 t)^{2} e^{(4 t^{2})}=9 t^{2} e^{4 t^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\sqrt{2xy},$ $x=3 t^{4}$ and $y=\ln{(2 t )},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$ for $t>0$ and $2 t>1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{y}{\sqrt{2xy}},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{2xy}}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{\ln{(2 t )}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{3 t^{4}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=12 t^{3},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\frac{1}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(\frac{\ln{(2 t )}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}})\cdot (12 t^{3})+(\frac{3 t^{4}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}})\cdot (\frac{1}{t}) \\  & =\frac{12 t^{3} \ln{(2 t )}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}}+\frac{3 t^{3}}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}} \\  & =\frac{3 t^{3} (\ln{(16 t^{4} )} + 1)}{\sqrt{2(3 t^{4})(\ln{(2 t )})}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\ln{(x y^{2} )},$ $x=\cos{(5 t )}$ and $y=\sin{(5 t )},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$ for $0<5 t<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{y^{2}}{x y^{2}}=\frac{1}{x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{2 x y}{x y^{2}}=\frac{2}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{1}{\cos{(5 t )}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{2}{\sin{(5 t )}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=- 5 \sin{(5 t )},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=5 \cos{(5 t )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(\frac{1}{\cos{(5 t )}})\cdot (- 5 \sin{(5 t )})+(\frac{2}{\sin{(5 t )}})\cdot (5 \cos{(5 t )}) \\  & =- \frac{5 \sin{(5 t )}}{\cos{(5 t )}} + (\frac{10 \cos{(5 t )}}{\sin{(5 t )}}) \\  & =- 5 \tan{(5 t )} + 10 \cot{(5 t )}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x^{2} e^{y},$ $x=t$ and $y=5 t^{4},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$

$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2 x e^{y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2 (t) e^{(5 t^{4})}=2 t e^{5 t^{4}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(t)^{2} e^{(5 t^{4})}=t^{2} e^{5 t^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=20 t^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =(2 t e^{5 t^{4}})\cdot (1)+(t^{2} e^{5 t^{4}})\cdot (20 t^{3}) \\  & =2 t e^{5 t^{4}} + (20 t^{5} e^{5 t^{4}}) \\  & =2 t (10 t^{4} + 1) e^{5 t^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y},$ $x=\cos{(4 s )}$ and $y=\sin{(4 s )},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s}$ where $\sin(4 s)\ne0$.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{1}{y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- \frac{x}{y^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{1}{\sin{(4 s )}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- \frac{\cos{(4 s )}}{\sin^{2}{(4 s )}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}=- 4 \sin{(4 s )},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s}=4 \cos{(4 s )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}s} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}s} \\  & =(\frac{1}{\sin{(4 s )}})\cdot (- 4 \sin{(4 s )})+(- \frac{\cos{(4 s )}}{\sin^{2}{(4 s )}})\cdot (4 \cos{(4 s )}) \\  & =-4 - \frac{4 \cos^{2}{(4 s )}}{\sin^{2}{(4 s )}} \\  & =- 4 \cot^{2}{(4 s )} - 4 \\  & =- 4 \csc^{2}{(4 s )}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=t^{3}$ and $y=t^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}} + e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(2 t + 1)^{4} e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=8 t + 4,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=2 t + 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}} + e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}})\cdot (8 t + 4)+((2 t + 1)^{4} e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}})\cdot (2 t + 2) \\  & =(8 t + 4) e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}} + ((t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2} (8 t + 4) e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}}) + ((2 t + 1)^{4} (2 t + 2) e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}}) \\  & =2 (2 t + 1) (2 (t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2} + (t + 1) (2 t + 1)^{3} + 2) e^{(t + 1)^{2} (2 t + 1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=(t + 1)^{3}$ and $y=(3 t + 1)^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}} + e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(t + 1)^{6} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3 (t + 1)^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=18 t + 6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}} + e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}})\cdot (3 (t + 1)^{2})+((t + 1)^{6} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}})\cdot (18 t + 6) \\  & =3 (t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}} + (3 (t + 1)^{5} (3 t + 1)^{2} e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}}) + ((t + 1)^{6} (18 t + 6) e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}}) \\  & =3 (t + 1)^{2} (2 (t + 1)^{4} (3 t + 1) + (t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2} + 1) e^{(t + 1)^{3} (3 t + 1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=(2 t - 3)^{2}$ and $y=(3 t - 3)^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2} e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}} + e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(2 t - 3)^{4} e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=8 t - 12,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=18 t - 18.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2} e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}} + e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}})\cdot (8 t - 12)+((2 t - 3)^{4} e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}})\cdot (18 t - 18) \\  & =(8 t - 12) e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}} + ((2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2} (8 t - 12) e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}}) + ((2 t - 3)^{4} (18 t - 18) e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}}) \\  & =2 (2 t - 3) (18 (t - 1)^{2} (2 t - 3)^{2} + 9 (t - 1) (2 t - 3)^{3} + 2) e^{(2 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 3)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}} + e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(2 t - 2)^{6} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6 (2 t - 2)^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=2 t + 6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}} + e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}})\cdot (6 (2 t - 2)^{2})+((2 t - 2)^{6} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}})\cdot (2 t + 6) \\  & =6 (2 t - 2)^{2} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}} + (6 (t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{5} e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}}) + ((2 t - 2)^{6} (2 t + 6) e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}}) \\  & =8 (t - 1)^{2} (16 (t - 1)^{4} (t + 3) + 24 (t - 1)^{3} (t + 3)^{2} + 3) e^{(t + 3)^{2} (2 t - 2)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=(3 t + 3)^{3}$ and $y=(3 t - 1)^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}} + e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(3 t + 3)^{6} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=9 (3 t + 3)^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=18 t - 6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}} + e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}})\cdot (9 (3 t + 3)^{2})+((3 t + 3)^{6} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}})\cdot (18 t - 6) \\  & =9 (3 t + 3)^{2} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}} + (9 (3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{5} e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}}) + ((3 t + 3)^{6} (18 t - 6) e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}}) \\  & =81 (t + 1)^{2} (54 (t + 1)^{4} (3 t - 1) + 27 (t + 1)^{3} (3 t - 1)^{2} + 1) e^{(3 t - 1)^{2} (3 t + 3)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=(3 t - 3)^{2}$ and $y=(3 t - 2)^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2} e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}} + e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(3 t - 3)^{4} e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=18 t - 18,\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=18 t - 12.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2} e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}} + e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}})\cdot (18 t - 18)+((3 t - 3)^{4} e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}})\cdot (18 t - 12) \\  & =(18 t - 18) e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}} + ((3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2} (18 t - 18) e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}}) + ((3 t - 3)^{4} (18 t - 12) e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}}) \\  & =18 (t - 1) (27 (t - 1)^{3} (3 t - 2) + 9 (t - 1)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2} + 1) e^{(3 t - 3)^{2} (3 t - 2)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Multivariable Function With One Independent Variable

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=x e^{x y},$ $x=(2 t - 2)^{3}$ and $y=(2 t + 3)^{2},$ compute $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/f0/f01b253f560405a8c0f4be8f8797c652fb0ddf774f4db110b8822313b8ac50f3.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with one independent variable $t,$ where $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=x y e^{x y} + e^{x y},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x^{2} e^{x y}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}} + e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(2 t - 2)^{6} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6 (2 t - 2)^{2},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=8 t + 12.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} \\  & =((2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}} + e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}})\cdot (6 (2 t - 2)^{2})+((2 t - 2)^{6} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}})\cdot (8 t + 12) \\  & =6 (2 t - 2)^{2} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}} + (6 (2 t - 2)^{5} (2 t + 3)^{2} e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}}) + ((2 t - 2)^{6} (8 t + 12) e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}}) \\  & =8 (t - 1)^{2} (32 (t - 1)^{4} (2 t + 3) + 24 (t - 1)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2} + 3) e^{(2 t - 2)^{3} (2 t + 3)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
